findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext values. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service and stored unencrypted, so any process on the host or anyone exploiting SSRF can harvest these long-lived IAM credentials.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption settings are specified, so the instance's attached storage may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.
No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with a publicly reachable web server, this widens the impact of SSRF into credential theft.

The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed to an internet gateway, and is attached to a security group open to 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH, so the host with embedded credentials is directly reachable from the internet.
Ingress rule allows TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound segmentation and facilitating data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no corresponding TLS listener, so web traffic to this host is transmitted in cleartext over the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (it is explicitly commented out), so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted and unprotected by KMS key access control.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume and specifies no encryption, so a copy of the volume data persists unencrypted and can be shared or restored without KMS controls.
The flow log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so VPC network flow records are stored unencrypted.
No public access block or bucket policy restricting public access is defined for the flow log bucket, risking exposure of network telemetry if an ACL or policy is later applied.
The bucket has no policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests, allowing log data to be read or written over cleartext HTTP.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the network boundary and directly exposing workloads to the internet.
